newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Republic puts Sentrachem on credit watch.
newsitem.headline: Republic puts Sentrachem on credit watch.

text.p: Rating agency Republic Ratings said on Monday it had placed chemicals group Sentrachem on credit watch with a view to a possible downgrade of its current long-term "A" rating.
Republic director Dave King said the move followed an increase in the group's financial risk profile in the year ended August 1996.
Gearing increased to 52 percent in the year from 14 percent in 1995, while interest cover deteriorated to 2.4 time cover from 5.4.
King said there were also concerns about shortfalls in the group's internal control environment.

Sentrachem announced last week that losses at its Sanachem subsidiary, which accounted for 10 percent of group operating profits last year, would impact substantially on group profitability in the 1997 financial year.

King said Republic would undertake a full scale review of Sentrachem over the next few weeks, but said that it did not necessarily follow that the group's rating would be downgraded as four of the group's five main operating companies were reportedly showing improved operating performances against last year.

Sentrachem's share price plunged 27 percent to an annual low of 900 cents last Thursday following the company's profit warning. On the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Monday morning, the shares were quoted at 930 cents.
